note.en: What you see: From the subcostal window the inferior vena cava runs as a dark tube from the liver into the right atrium. In M mode its walls move with breath: collapsing inward on inspiration during spontaneous breathing and expanding during mechanical inspiration. A small collapsing cava suggests low right sided pressure and fluid tolerance, while a large fixed cava suggests high right sided pressure. The hepatic vein joins nearby and must not be mistaken for the main trunk.

steps.en: What you see: From the subcostal window the inferior vena cava runs as a dark tube from the liver into the right atrium. In M mode its walls move with breath: collapsing inward on inspiration during spontaneous breathing and expanding during mechanical inspiration. A small collapsing cava suggests low right sided pressure and fluid tolerance, while a large fixed cava suggests high right sided pressure. The hepatic vein joins nearby and must not be mistaken for the main trunk.
Landmarks to confirm: Inferior vena cava trunk, right atrium entry, hepatic vein branch, liver as the window.

Common mistakes and correction: Mistaking the aorta for the cava: the aorta pulses and never collapses, while the cava varies with breath. Off axis cut that overstates collapse: keep the beam perpendicular at 1 to 2 cm from the junction. Sampling a hepatic vein branch instead of the main trunk: track the vessel to the atrial entry before measuring.

Normal values with units: Measure at 1 to 2 cm from the junction with the right atrium. A diameter of 2.1 cm or less with collapse of 50 percent or more on sniff marks normal right atrial pressure of 0 to 5 mmHg. A diameter above 2.1 cm with collapse below 50 percent marks raised right atrial pressure of 10 to 20 mmHg. Intermediate patterns need clinical correlation.

Pitfalls: Positive pressure ventilation reverses the breathing pattern, so apply the rule only to spontaneously breathing patients and seek senior guidance in ventilated cases. Raised abdominal pressure and severe tricuspid regurgitation distend the cava regardless of volume. Never give large fluid volumes on the cava alone; integrate pulse, pressure, lungs and clinical context.

todo.en: How to get it step by step: From the subcostal four chamber, rotate into the sagittal plane just right of midline through the liver. Follow the cava to its entry into the right atrium. Measure perpendicular to its long axis at 1 to 2 cm from the junction. Record M mode across a full breath, adding a sniff when the patient can cooperate. Keep the beam perpendicular, since an oblique cut overstates collapse.

q.en: How is the cava window obtained?

o.en: Sagittal just right of midline through the liver to the atrial entry

why.en: A sagittal plane just right of midline through the liver opens the cava to its atrial entry.

o.en: Perpendicular to the trunk at 1 to 2 cm from the junction

why.en: Guidance places measurement perpendicular to the trunk at 1 to 2 cm from the atrial junction.

q.en: Which pattern marks normal right atrial pressure?

o.en: 2.1 cm or less with 50 percent or more collapse marks 0 to 5 mmHg
Any size with any collapse is normal
A fixed cava marks low pressure

why.en: A cava of 2.1 cm or less collapsing 50 percent or more marks pressure of 0 to 5 mmHg.
